title: Inertia of a body with its own mark in a weakly pinned field of oscillator cells

key_results.statement: Ring and cubic torus, every $L$, $M\to\infty$ first, every level and both branches under (6.4), $P$ near 0: $E_{k,\sigma}(P)=E_f+\sigma\sqrt{M_k^2\bar F^2+\tau^2\sin^2P}+E^{(2)}_{k,\sigma}(P)+O(\delta F^3)$, even in $P$, with $\bar F=F_0+F_2w_0$.

$E^{(2)}_{k,\sigma}(P)=-M_k^2\langle\!\langle\cos^2\vartheta/(E+\sigma[\omega(P-Q)-\omega(P)])+\sin^2\vartheta/(E-\sigma[\omega(P-Q)+\omega(P)])\rangle\!\rangle$, $\vartheta=\frac12[\theta(P)+\theta(P-Q)]$, a spectral sum over one- and two-quantum field states (6.1).

$\sigma=-1$: isolated and analytic in $P$, $\delta F$ if $\Omega_q>\omega_k(q_1)-\varepsilon_k$ for all $q$ (implied by $\tau^2\le2\varepsilon_kc_0$); $\sigma=+1$: second-order coefficients analytic near $P=0$ under (U) (implied by $\Omega_{\max}<\varepsilon_k$, or $\Omega_{\max}<2\varepsilon_k$ if $F_2=0$); not isolated at second order as $L\to\infty$ if a function of (U) changes sign.

$C^{(1)}_{k,\sigma}=\sigma M_k\bar F$ for every $\tau$; $C^{\rm mark}_{k,\sigma}=E^{(2)}_{k,\sigma}(0)=-M_k^2(F_1^2G_0/2+2F_2^2J_2)(1+\delta_C)$, $\delta_C=\tau^2\langle\!\langle\sin^2Q/[E^2(E-2\sigma\varepsilon_k)]\rangle\!\rangle/\langle\!\langle1/E\rangle\!\rangle+O(\tau^4)$; the held mark is strictly negative.

Both graphs, every $L,\ell$, $\tau>0$: $I^{(1)}_{k,\sigma}=C^{(1)}_{k,\sigma}/\tau^2$ for every level, both branches and every $r$; $I^{\rm mark}_{k,\sigma}=-\varepsilon_k^2E^{(2)\prime\prime}_{k,\sigma}(0)/\tau^4$; a single $v$ exists iff $\rho_{k,\sigma}=\tau^2I^{\rm mark}/C^{\rm mark}=1$ for all $k,\sigma$, and then $v=\tau$.

Ring, $L\gg\ell$, under (6.4), up to relative $O(\delta_\ell)$: $C^{\rm mark}=-\frac{M_k^2\ell}{4c_0^2}(F_1^2+\frac{F_2^2}{2c_0})$, $\zeta=F_2^2/2c_0$, $E^{(2)\prime\prime}(0)=-\frac{2\tau^2}{\varepsilon_k^2}C^{\rm mark}[1-\frac{r^2}{2}-\sigma\varepsilon_kR]$, with $R=O(\ln^2\ell/c_0\ell)$.

Ring, $L\gg\ell$, every (G2) grip, every level and both branches under (6.4), every $r>0$: $\rho_{k,\sigma}=2-r^2-2\sigma\varepsilon_kR+O(\delta_\ell)$; at leading order in $1/\ell$, $I^{\rm mark}=(2-r^2)C^{\rm mark}/\tau^2$, so one $v$ for $I^{(1)}$ and $I^{\rm mark}$ for every level and both branches exists iff $r=1$, with $v=\tau=c_0$; first difference $(1-r^2)C^{\rm mark}/\tau^2$.

Both graphs, every $L,\ell$, under (6.4): $\rho_{k,+}-\rho_{k,-}=-4\varepsilon_kR[1+O((c_0^2+\tau^2(1+r^2))/\varepsilon_k^2)]$, so for $\varepsilon_k\gg c_0$, $\varepsilon_k^2\gg\tau^2(1+r^2)$ no single $v$ exists at second order at any $r$ ($r=1$ included) and any finite $\ell$; in the heavy regime ($\varepsilon_kR\gg1+r^2$, $\tau^2\ll\varepsilon_kc_0$) $I^{\rm mark}=I^{(1)}Y_k$, $\rho_{k,\sigma}=-2\sigma\varepsilon_kR$ at leading order.

Both graphs, every $L,\ell,r$, second order in $\delta F$ with $F_1,F_2$ counted alike, weights (2.8): $E''\Delta W=\frac{\tau^2F_1\Delta\phi}{F_0}[1-F_2w_0/F_0-2\sigma M_kF_2G_0]$, the same for every level and both branches at this order iff $F_2=0$; for $F_2=0$ the first level dependence comes from $I^{\rm mark}$ at relative order $F_1^2$ via (6.12): on the ring at leading order in $1/\ell$ it vanishes only at $r=\sqrt2$, on the cubic torus at no computed $r$ once two lower levels are isolated (6.15).

Grips of fixed shape through relative order $\beta^2$, weights (2.8): $E''\Delta W=\frac{\tau^2F_1\Delta\phi}{F_0}[1-F_2w_0/F_0-2\sigma M_kF_2G_0-I^{\rm mark}/I^{(1)}]$; on the ring at leading order in $1/\ell$ it is level and branch independent iff $(2-r^2)F_1^2=4F_0F_2$ (square grip iff $r=1$, linear grip only at $r=\sqrt2$); for $\varepsilon_k\gg c_0,\tau\sqrt{1+r^2}$ and levels whose $M_k^2$ differ by more than the error of (6.10), no (G2) grip gives it at finite $\ell$ on either graph.

Both graphs, under (6.4): with $E^{(2)}=-M_k^2(F_1^2S_1+F_2^2S_2)$, $\rho_{k,\sigma}=(S_1\rho_1+\xi c_0S_2\rho_2)/(S_1+\xi c_0S_2)$, $\xi=F_2^2/(c_0F_1^2)$, so $\rho_{k,\sigma}=1$ iff $\xi=\xi^*_{k,\sigma}=S_1(1-\rho_1)/(c_0S_2(\rho_2-1))\ge0$; the bracket of (6.12) is $1-F_2w_0/F_0-\sigma(\varepsilon_kF_1^2G_0/F_0^2)(2y-t_{k,\sigma})$ with $y=F_0F_2/F_1^2$, $t=-(\varepsilon_k^2/\tau^2)S_1''(0)/G_0$.

Cubic torus, numerical ($L=64$, $\ell=8$, convergence checked), every (G2) grip, $r\in[0.1,3]$, $\varepsilon_k/c_0\in[0.1,64]$: one $v$ with $I^{(1)}=C^{(1)}/v^2$ and $I^{\rm mark}=C^{\rm mark}/v^2$ on the nonempty set $\mathcal S$ of isolated states exists iff $\mathcal S$ is the lower branch of a single level with $\varepsilon_k$ in a window (about $[0.93,2.61]c_0$ at $r=1$) and $\xi=\xi^*_{k,-}$, then $v=\tau$; once two states are isolated no grip and no computed $r$ ($r=1$ included) give one $v$, since $\rho_{k,+}<1$ and $\xi^*_{k,-}$ is strictly monotone in $\varepsilon_k$; where (U) begins $\varepsilon_kR\le0.80$.

Cubic torus, same setting, relative order $\beta^2$, weights (2.8): $E''\Delta W$ is the same on $\mathcal S$ iff $\sigma\varepsilon_k(2y-t_{k,\sigma})$ is; no (G2) grip achieves this if $\mathcal S$ contains both branches of two levels or three lower levels where $\varphi=\varepsilon t_-$ is strictly convex (all computed $\varepsilon_k$ for $r\le1.25$); for two isolated states exactly one $y$ works, depending on the levels and $r$; the linear grip fails for any two lower levels and for both branches of one level when $r\le2$; the square grip is not singled out.

open_issues: Cubic torus: (6.14) and (6.15) rest on lattice sums evaluated on a grid (r in [0.1, 3], ε_k/c_0 in [0.1, 64], L = 64, ℓ = 8, with a convergence check); between grid points they rest on the monotonicity and convexity found on the grid, and above 64c_0 on (6.10); the band where the lower-branch gap is below m_h/2, and r > 3, were not computed.
Branch σ=+1 beyond second order: lower-branch states with three or more quanta can be degenerate with the level; whether the exact level is isolated as L→∞ is not settled.
The weight of the moving body is taken from (2.8) without corrections in τ; (6.11) and (6.12) rest on this.
On the ring the expansion parameter grows like ℓ, so (6.8)–(6.12) need δF to shrink as ℓ grows; the regime M_k F_1² G_0 ∼ F_0 is open.

consistency_checks.check: Held limit τ→0: E^(2)(0) equals the second-order part of the mark cost in (2.6)
Bare body δF=0, F0=1: E''(0)=στ²/M_k as in (6.7) of 04-ilang-time/06-inertia-internal-energy
Dimensions of costs, inertias, r and E''ΔW
